_comment: Tier-2 for skfem point_source#5, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / meshio 5.3.5. Claim: VTK output wants 3D-padded points but meshio 5.3.5 does NOT raise on an (N,2) array -- meshio.Mesh constructs, the writer prints 'Warning: VTU requires 3D points, but 2D points given. Appending 0 third component.' on stdout and writes the file anyway, and there is no 'expected ndarray of shape (N, 3)' ValueError. Ran: MeshTri().refined(3) with a point-source solution as point_data, written once with raw (81,2) points and once z-padded, both read back. Printed: neither the constructor nor the writer raises; the file is written; the read-back point array has 3 columns against the 2 supplied, with the third all zero. NEW, and what makes this hard to catch: the notice is NOT a Python warning -- warnings.catch_warnings records an empty list, so simplefilter('error') cannot turn it into an exception -- and it escapes contextlib.redirect_stdout, so a caller cannot capture it that way either. The padded write round-trips its points exactly and agrees with the unpadded one, and the point data survives; comparing what came back against what you meant to send is the check that works. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 builds the first meshio.Mesh from z-padded (81,3) points ('supplied') instead of the raw (81,2) m.p.T array -- the documented fix. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / meshio 5.3.5: the unmutated run matches all 13 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 leaves meshio nothing to append, so the stdout notice 'VTU requires 3D points, but 2D points given' is never printed and 'meshio_added_a_column_you_never_supplied=True' flips to False, and the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
expect_in_output: VTU requires 3D points, but 2D points given
